title: Brushes and a two-beat bass drum on the spirituals
summary: He used wire brushes on the church-style record to keep volume under his vocals and the muted horns.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: See on this record you know where you play the Spiritus you play the wire brushes. Yeah. And two beat on the bass drum. Yeah that's right. But this is the first time you ever played in the church was it?
Yeah. First time the whole band in fact. Yeah. How come that you used the brushes on all them? You just thought that would fit the edge?
Well it was kind of softened down a little bit instead of using the sticks.
But you never heard anybody use these uh, play this way in churches when you were young?

Never did. Never heard of a jazz band in my life being in the church. Yeah. Never heard of a jazz band in Oakland of the spiritual, felt like I was on a string. See? Yeah. But that actual wire brush and two beat on that, you never heard that before? No, no. That was just something I had this big...
I've heard quite a few people doing that now.

Yeah, I see. I've got to do something to kind of keep the volume down low under my singing, you know, and under their mutes. Because you can't get the exact riff out of sticks like you want, like you can't get out the brushes. Yeah, I know what you mean. So you see the brushes give a kind of a sweeping effect. Yeah.
